misconception_description: Student believes that the body of an if-statement executes repeatedly as long as the condition holds.

solutions.generated_code:
program CariTerkecil
kamus
  n, i, x, terkecil : integer
algoritma
  input(n)
  i <- 1
  if i <= n then
    input(x)
    if i == 1 then
      terkecil <- x
    else
      if x < terkecil then
        terkecil <- x
      endif
    endif
    i <- i + 1
  endif
  output(terkecil)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student replaced the for loop with an if-statement, believing it will repeatedly execute and iterate through all elements of the list as long as index < len(list1). They increment index within the if-block and check each element against min_val. In reality, the if-statement only executes once, so the function will only compare the first two elements (list1[0] and list1[1]) and return an incorrect result for lists where the minimum is not among the first two elements. The student is confident this works because they believe the if-statement will keep re-evaluating and executing its body until the condition becomes false, similar to a while loop.
